Build legacy-compatible fixed-width text reports

Source: R/api-tables.R
build_fixed_reports.Rd

Build legacy-compatible fixed-width text reports

Usage

build_fixed_reports(
  bias_results,
  target_facet = NULL,
  branch = c("facets", "original"),
  df_method = c("facets", "classical")
)

Arguments

bias_results

Output from estimate_bias().

target_facet

Optional target facet for pairwise contrast table.

branch

Output branch: "facets" keeps the legacy-compatible fixed-width layout; "original" returns compact sectioned fixed-width text for report drafts.

df_method

Pairwise df convention: "facets" (modified Rasch-Welch, integer part, matching FACETS 4.5.0) or "classical" (former continuous df).

Value

A named list with class mfrm_fixed_reports (and a branch-specific subclass mfrm_fixed_reports_<branch>):

  • bias_fixed: fixed-width interaction table text

  • pairwise_fixed: fixed-width pairwise contrast text

  • pairwise_table: underlying pairwise data.frame

  • branch: character scalar "original" or "facets" echoing which fixed-width style was rendered

  • style: character scalar carrying the resolved style preset used when building the text artifact

  • interaction_label: human-readable label for the interaction that drove the bias run ("Rater x Criterion"-style); NA when no bias rows are available

  • target_facet: character scalar identifying which facet was used as the target facet for pairwise contrasts; NA when no pairwise contrasts were requested or available

Details

This function generates plain-text, fixed-width output intended to be read in console/log environments or exported into text reports.

The pairwise section (Table 14 style) is only generated for 2-way bias runs. For higher-order interactions (interaction_facets length >= 3), the function returns the bias table text and a note explaining why pairwise contrasts were skipped.

Pairwise calculation

For each target element, compare its local measure in two contexts. If the target has predictor sign s, its local measure is target + bias/s; the contrast is Context1 minus Context2. A negatively oriented rater therefore has local severity severity - bias. TargetSign comes from the saved bias result's orientation_review. Missing orientation withholds local measures, contrasts and tail areas; it is not inferred from a facet name.

SE1 and SE2 are conditional cell-information SEs with baseline calibration held fixed. The contrast SE is sqrt(SE1^2 + SE2^2) under conditional independence of the two cells. Calibration uncertainty and cross-cell covariance are not propagated. Target S.E. describes the original target estimate separately and is not added to the conditional local SE; a fixed target can still have uncertain local bias.

The default df_method = "facets" uses the modified Rasch-Welch formula described in the FACETS t-statistics manual (von Davier, 2025). Writing v1 = SE1^2, v2 = SE2^2 and n1, n2 for weighted counts, its df is (v1+v2)^2 * (n1+n2-2) / ((n1+n2+2) * (v1^2/(n1+1)+v2^2/(n2+1))). The tail area uses its integer part, matching executed FACETS 4.5.0 unequal-count examples. Values are stabilized to ten decimal places before truncation to avoid numerical noise at integer boundaries. DFUnrounded retains the original continuous value. df_method = "classical" retains the former Welch-Satterthwaite reference with n1-1, n2-1 and no integer truncation. DFMethod and DFBasis identify the choice; equal counts alone cannot distinguish the formulas. ObsN1 and ObsN2 are raw row counts. Both weighted counts must exceed one, both SEs must be positive and finite, and the final df must be positive. Otherwise the screen remains unavailable. Fractional weights follow the same rule but are outside the executed comparison. These are conditional screens, not calibrated fairness tests or general FACETS equivalence.

Saved pairwise results

Current tables carry CalculationVersion = 3. Recreate older fixed or pairwise reports using build_fixed_reports() or bias_pairwise_report(). If the bias bundle predates baseline-score corrections or lacks orientation, recreate estimate_bias() from the saved fit and current diagnostics first. No main calibration refit is needed. Keep historical values separately; summaries and fixed-report plots reject older pairwise calculations.

Interpreting output

  • bias_fixed: fixed-width table of interaction effects.

  • pairwise_fixed: pairwise contrast text (2-way only).

  • pairwise_table: structured contrast table.

  • interaction_label: facets used for the bias run.

Typical workflow

  1. Run estimate_bias().

  2. Build text bundle with build_fixed_reports(...).

  3. Use summary()/plot() for quick checks, then export text blocks.

Preferred route for new analyses

For new reporting workflows, prefer bias_interaction_report() and build_apa_outputs(). Use build_fixed_reports() when a fixed-width text artifact is specifically required for a compatibility handoff.

See also

estimate_bias(), build_apa_outputs(), bias_interaction_report(), mfrmr_reports_and_tables, mfrmr_compatibility_layer

Examples

toy <- load_mfrmr_data("example_bias")
fit <- fit_mfrm(toy, "Person", c("Rater", "Criterion"), "Score", method = "JML", maxit = 300)
diag <- diagnose_mfrm(fit, residual_pca = "none")
bias <- estimate_bias(fit, diag, facet_a = "Rater", facet_b = "Criterion", max_iter = 2)
fixed <- build_fixed_reports(bias)
fixed_original <- build_fixed_reports(bias, branch = "original")
summary(fixed)
